question: Is the spoon ungraspable, or ungraspable where the scene parks it?
row_under_test: req_demo_video (DRAFT) -- spoon_placed is 0/10 and task_success is all(subgoals), so this sub-goal caps the row by itself. req_mujoco_sim (READY) is the row that OWNS the scene geometry under test.
restates: F-SPOON-POSE-INFEASIBLE-001, and evidence/cutlery_approach.json which uses it as a negative control
method: snapshot the arm at its own spoon_descend waypoint, teleport the spoon along the drawer axis, re-solve the grasp at each station, and apply run()'s own grip test verbatim. Nothing on disk is changed: envs/dinner_table.xml is untouched and the teleport lives inside this probe.

C1_agrees_with_reference_implementation.what: on every seed, both waypoints, this probe's min_clear_dz and jaw_below_handle_top must equal what measure_grasp_feasibility.run() returns when run NOW. This is the instrument check: the first two versions of this probe failed it and were corrected, not published.

C2_on_disk_evidence_is_stale.what: evidence/grasp_feasibility.json must DISAGREE with both the reference implementation and this probe. If it agreed, the finding below would be a probe bug, not a stale file. C1 and C2 have to pass TOGETHER: C1 says the instrument is right, C2 says the record is not.

C3_pushing_spoon_toward_drawer_front_doe.what: drawer_front is the wall the arm reaches over, so moving the spoon toward it must not improve the grasp. A probe that improved in both directions would be reading solver noise.
